claim: Fabry disease (FD) is a life-threatening X-linked lysosomal storage disorder caused by α-galactosidase A (α-GAL) deficiency.
source: Fabry disease (FD) is a life-threatening X-linked lysosomal storage disorder caused by α-galactosidase A (α-GAL) deficiency.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about Fabry disease.

claim: Small fiber pathology and pain are major FD symptoms of unknown pathophysiology.
source: Small fiber pathology and pain are major FD symptoms of unknown pathophysiology.
evidence: This statement is supported by established clinical knowledge about Fabry disease symptoms.

claim: α-GAL deficient mice (GLA KO) age-dependently accumulate globotriaosylceramide (Gb3) in dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons.
source: α-GAL deficient mice (GLA KO) age-dependently accumulate globotriaosylceramide (Gb3) in dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons paralleled by endoplasmic stress and apoptosis as contributors to skin denervation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript, including immunohistochemistry and confocal microscopy results.

claim: Gb3 accumulation in DRG neurons is paralleled by endoplasmic stress and apoptosis as contributors to skin denervation.
source: α-GAL deficient mice (GLA KO) age-dependently accumulate globotriaosylceramide (Gb3) in dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons paralleled by endoplasmic stress and apoptosis as contributors to skin denervation.
evidence: This is supported by BiP expression analysis and caspase 3 assay data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Old GLA KO mice show increased TRPV1 protein in DRG neurons.
source: Old GLA KO mice show increased TRPV1 protein in DRG neurons and heat hypersensitivity upon i.pl. capsaicin.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data showing TRPV1 immunoreactivity in DRG neurons.

claim: Old GLA KO mice show heat hypersensitivity upon intraplantar capsaicin injection.
source: Old GLA KO mice show increased TRPV1 protein in DRG neurons and heat hypersensitivity upon i.pl. capsaicin.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral testing data showing thermal withdrawal latencies after capsaicin injection.

claim: GLA KO mice are protected from heat and mechanical hypersensitivity in neuropathic and inflammatory pain models based on reduced neuronal Ih and Nav1.7 currents.
source: In turn, GLA KO mice are protected from heat and mechanical hypersensitivity in neuropathic and inflammatory pain models based on reduced neuronal Ih and Nav1.7 currents.
evidence: This is supported by patch-clamp electrophysiology data and behavioral testing in CCI and CFA models.

claim: In vitro α-GAL silencing increases intracellular Gb3 accumulation paralleled by loss of Nav1.7 currents.
source: We show that in vitro α-GAL silencing increases intracellular Gb3 accumulation paralleled by loss of Nav1.7 currents, which is reversed by incubation with agalsidase-α and lucerastat.
evidence: This is supported by shRNA experiments in HEK cells with immunocytochemistry and patch-clamp analysis.

claim: Loss of Nav1.7 currents after α-GAL silencing is reversed by incubation with agalsidase-α and lucerastat.
source: We show that in vitro α-GAL silencing increases intracellular Gb3 accumulation paralleled by loss of Nav1.7 currents, which is reversed by incubation with agalsidase-α and lucerastat.
evidence: This is supported by patch-clamp analysis of HEK cells treated with agalsidase-α and lucerastat.

claim: There is a direct Gb3 effect on neuronal integrity and ion channel function as a potential mechanism underlying pain and small fiber pathology in FD.
source: We provide first evidence of a direct Gb3 effect on neuronal integrity and ion channel function as potential mechanism underlying pain and small fiber pathology in FD.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined experimental data showing Gb3 accumulation, ion channel dysfunction, and reversibility with treatment.

claim: Thermal hyposensitivity and pain based on small nerve fiber pathology are cardinal neurological symptoms of Fabry disease.
source: Thermal hyposensitivity and pain based on small nerve fiber pathology are cardinal neurological symptoms of the progressive and life-threatening X-linked Fabry disease (FD) (Zarate and Hopkin, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Zarate and Hopkin, 2008.

claim: Genetically caused reduction or loss of α-galactosidase A (α-GAL) with consecutive lysosomal accumulation of globotriaosylceramide (Gb3) has long been considered the pathophysiological key event in FD.
source: While genetically caused reduction or loss of α-galactosidase A (α-GAL) with consecutive lysosomal accumulation of globotriaosylceramide (Gb3) has long been considered the pathophysiological key event in FD (Romeo and Migeon, 1970), the mechanisms underlying sensory impairment, pain, and denervation remain unclear.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Romeo and Migeon, 1970.

claim: The mechanisms underlying sensory impairment, pain, and denervation in FD remain unclear.
source: While genetically caused reduction or loss of α-galactosidase A (α-GAL) with consecutive lysosomal accumulation of globotriaosylceramide (Gb3) has long been considered the pathophysiological key event in FD (Romeo and Migeon, 1970), the mechanisms underlying sensory impairment, pain, and denervation remain unclear.
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap in the field.

claim: Men more than women with FD report reduction in cold and warm sensation over time.
source: Men more than women with FD report reduction in cold and warm sensation over time, which is reflected by increased thermal perception thresholds and paralleled by loss of intraepidermal innervation (Üçeyler et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Üçeyler et al., 2011.

claim: Reduction in cold and warm sensation in FD patients is reflected by increased thermal perception thresholds and paralleled by loss of intraepidermal innervation.
source: Men more than women with FD report reduction in cold and warm sensation over time, which is reflected by increased thermal perception thresholds and paralleled by loss of intraepidermal innervation (Üçeyler et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Üçeyler et al., 2011.

claim: FD patients report mainly episodic, acral, burning pain triggered by heat, fever, or physical activity starting in early childhood.
source: Starting in early childhood, patients also report mainly episodic, acral, burning pain triggered by heat, fever, or physical activity (Üçeyler et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Üçeyler et al., 2014.

claim: Potential Gb3 deposits have been found in dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons.
source: The finding of potential Gb3 deposits in dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons (Gadoth and Sandbank, 1983; Lakomá et al., 2016; Marshall et al., 2010) and the presence of peripheral neuropathy mostly of the small fiber type (Üçeyler et al., 2011) supports the hypothesis of a pathophysiological mechanism involving Gb3 accumulation.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Gadoth and Sandbank, 1983; Lakomá et al., 2016; Marshall et al., 2010.

claim: Peripheral neuropathy in FD is mostly of the small fiber type.
source: The finding of potential Gb3 deposits in dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons (Gadoth and Sandbank, 1983; Lakomá et al., 2016; Marshall et al., 2010) and the presence of peripheral neuropathy mostly of the small fiber type (Üçeyler et al., 2011) supports the hypothesis of a pathophysiological mechanism involving Gb3 accumulation.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Üçeyler et al., 2011.

claim: The largest and oldest cohort (>24 months) of α-GAL deficient (GLA KO) mice showed age-dependent development of thermal hyposensitivity mirroring the clinical phenotype.
source: Having investigated the largest and oldest cohort (>24 months) reported thus far for the α-GAL deficient (GLA KO) mouse model of FD, we previously described an age-dependent development of thermal hyposensitivity mirroring the clinical phenotype (Üçeyler et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Üçeyler et al., 2016.

claim: Young GLA KO mice have larger DRG neurons compared to young WT mice.
source: First, we examined DRG neuron size by analysing neuronal area (Figure 1A–D) and found larger DRG neurons in young GLA KO compared to young WT mice (p<0.01; Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of neuronal area shown in Figure 1E with statistical significance p<0.01.

claim: Neurons of old GLA KO mice are larger compared to old WT mice.
source: Neurons of old GLA KO mice were larger compared to old WT (p<0.001) and young GLA KO mice (p<0.001; Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of neuronal area shown in Figure 1E with statistical significance p<0.001.

claim: Neurons of old GLA KO mice are larger compared to young GLA KO mice.
source: Neurons of old GLA KO mice were larger compared to old WT (p<0.001) and young GLA KO mice (p<0.001; Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of neuronal area shown in Figure 1E with statistical significance p<0.001.

claim: Intraneuronal deposits are present in DRG neurons of young GLA KO mice.
source: We assessed semithin sections and found intraneuronal deposits in young and even more so in old GLA KO mice, while DRG neurons from wildtype (WT) mice displayed normal histology (Figure 1F–I).
evidence: This is supported by toluidine blue staining of semithin sections shown in Figure 1F-I.

claim: Intraneuronal deposits are more prominent in old GLA KO mice compared to young GLA KO mice.
source: We assessed semithin sections and found intraneuronal deposits in young and even more so in old GLA KO mice, while DRG neurons from wildtype (WT) mice displayed normal histology (Figure 1F–I).
evidence: This is supported by toluidine blue staining of semithin sections shown in Figure 1F-I.

claim: DRG neurons from wildtype (WT) mice display normal histology.
source: We assessed semithin sections and found intraneuronal deposits in young and even more so in old GLA KO mice, while DRG neurons from wildtype (WT) mice displayed normal histology (Figure 1F–I).
evidence: This is supported by toluidine blue staining of semithin sections shown in Figure 1F-I.

claim: Marked Gb3 immunoreactivity is present in DRG of old GLA KO mice.
source: We then applied antibodies against CD77 to detect Gb3 and saw marked immunoreaction in DRG of old GLA KO mice, which was not detectable in young mice and in WT littermates (Figure 1J–M).
evidence: This is supported by CD77 immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 1J-M.

claim: Gb3 immunoreactivity is not detectable in young GLA KO mice.
source: We then applied antibodies against CD77 to detect Gb3 and saw marked immunoreaction in DRG of old GLA KO mice, which was not detectable in young mice and in WT littermates (Figure 1J–M).
evidence: This is supported by CD77 immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 1J-M.

claim: Gb3 immunoreactivity is not detectable in WT littermates.
source: We then applied antibodies against CD77 to detect Gb3 and saw marked immunoreaction in DRG of old GLA KO mice, which was not detectable in young mice and in WT littermates (Figure 1J–M).
evidence: This is supported by CD77 immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 1J-M.

claim: Gb3 immunoreactivity is not restricted to neurons, but is also present extra-neurally.
source: Interestingly, Gb3 immunoreactivity was not restricted to neurons, but was also present extra-neurally (Figure 1M, arrowheads).
evidence: This is supported by CD77 immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 1M.

claim: Gb3 is mainly located in the cytoplasm of DRG neurons of old GLA KO mice.
source: Applying confocal microscopy and co-immunoreaction with antibodies against β-(ΙΙΙ)-tubulin, we found that Gb3 is mainly located in the cytoplasm of DRG neurons of old GLA KO mice but also in the very proximal parts of sensory axons, in extra-neural connective tissue, and cellular membranes (Video 1).
evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Video 1.

claim: Gb3 is located in the very proximal parts of sensory axons in old GLA KO mice.
source: Applying confocal microscopy and co-immunoreaction with antibodies against β-(ΙΙΙ)-tubulin, we found that Gb3 is mainly located in the cytoplasm of DRG neurons of old GLA KO mice but also in the very proximal parts of sensory axons, in extra-neural connective tissue, and cellular membranes (Video 1).
evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Video 1.

claim: Gb3 is located in extra-neural connective tissue in old GLA KO mice.
source: Applying confocal microscopy and co-immunoreaction with antibodies against β-(ΙΙΙ)-tubulin, we found that Gb3 is mainly located in the cytoplasm of DRG neurons of old GLA KO mice but also in the very proximal parts of sensory axons, in extra-neural connective tissue, and cellular membranes (Video 1).
evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Video 1.

claim: Gb3 is located in cellular membranes in old GLA KO mice.
source: Applying confocal microscopy and co-immunoreaction with antibodies against β-(ΙΙΙ)-tubulin, we found that Gb3 is mainly located in the cytoplasm of DRG neurons of old GLA KO mice but also in the very proximal parts of sensory axons, in extra-neural connective tissue, and cellular membranes (Video 1).
evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Video 1.

claim: BiP was homogeneously distributed in neurons of young GLA KO and WT mice.
source: BiP was homogeneously distributed in neurons of young GLA KO and WT mice (data not shown) and in old WT mice (Figure 1N).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 1N for old WT mice.

claim: BiP was homogeneously distributed in neurons of old WT mice.
source: BiP was homogeneously distributed in neurons of young GLA KO and WT mice (data not shown) and in old WT mice (Figure 1N).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 1N.

claim: In neurons of old GLA KO mice, condensed BiP was located within and around the nucleus indicating enhanced endoplasmic stress.
source: In contrast, in neurons of old GLA KO mice, condensed BiP was located within and around the nucleus (Figure 1O) indicating enhanced endoplasmic stress.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 1O and inferred from the known role of BiP in endoplasmic stress.

claim: Young GLA KO mice show a marked reduction of cutaneous innervation compared to young WT mice.
source: We quantified intraepidermal nerve fiber density (IENFD) in skin obtained from mouse hind paws and found a marked reduction of cutaneous innervation in young and old GLA KO mice compared to their WT littermates (Figure 2A–D), surpassing the physiological reduction of IENFD with aging (p<0.001 each, Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of IENFD shown in Figure 2E with statistical significance p<0.001.

claim: Old GLA KO mice show a marked reduction of cutaneous innervation compared to old WT mice.
source: We quantified intraepidermal nerve fiber density (IENFD) in skin obtained from mouse hind paws and found a marked reduction of cutaneous innervation in young and old GLA KO mice compared to their WT littermates (Figure 2A–D), surpassing the physiological reduction of IENFD with aging (p<0.001 each, Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of IENFD shown in Figure 2E with statistical significance p<0.001.

claim: The reduction of IENFD in GLA KO mice surpasses the physiological reduction of IENFD with aging.
source: We quantified intraepidermal nerve fiber density (IENFD) in skin obtained from mouse hind paws and found a marked reduction of cutaneous innervation in young and old GLA KO mice compared to their WT littermates (Figure 2A–D), surpassing the physiological reduction of IENFD with aging (p<0.001 each, Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of IENFD shown in Figure 2E with statistical significance p<0.001.

claim: No Gb3 depositions were found in the sciatic nerve of old GLA KO and WT mice.
source: Furthermore, we assessed whether Gb3 accumulates not only in DRG, but also in axons of the sciatic nerve and in skin. We did not find any Gb3 depositions in the sciatic nerve (Figure 2F–K) or footpad skin (Figure 2L–Q) of old GLA KO and WT mice.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 2F-K.

claim: No Gb3 depositions were found in footpad skin of old GLA KO and WT mice.
source: Furthermore, we assessed whether Gb3 accumulates not only in DRG, but also in axons of the sciatic nerve and in skin. We did not find any Gb3 depositions in the sciatic nerve (Figure 2F–K) or footpad skin (Figure 2L–Q) of old GLA KO and WT mice.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 2L-Q.

claim: DRG neuron cultures of old GLA KO mice in the naïve state display a higher percentage of caspase 3 positive neurons compared to old WT mice.
source: DRG neuron cultures of old GLA KO mice in the naïve state displayed a higher percentage of caspase 3 positive neurons compared to old WT mice (p<0.001, Figure 3E) indicating enhanced apoptosis.
evidence: This is supported by NucView 488 Caspase 3 Enzyme Substrate Assay data shown in Figure 3E with statistical significance p<0.001.

claim: Higher percentage of caspase 3 positive neurons in old GLA KO mice indicates enhanced apoptosis.
source: DRG neuron cultures of old GLA KO mice in the naïve state displayed a higher percentage of caspase 3 positive neurons compared to old WT mice (p<0.001, Figure 3E) indicating enhanced apoptosis.
evidence: This is inferred from the known role of caspase 3 in apoptosis.

claim: Positive control neurons of both genotypes incubated with 500 nM staurosporine for 16 hr showed a higher percentage of caspase 3 positive neurons compared to cultured DRG neurons in the naïve state.
source: Additionally, positive control neurons of both genotypes incubated with 500 nM staurosporine for 16 hr showed a higher percentage of caspase 3 positive neurons compared to cultured DRG neurons in the naïve state (p<0.05 each, Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by NucView 488 Caspase 3 Enzyme Substrate Assay data shown in Figure 3E with statistical significance p<0.05.

claim: Cultured DRG neurons of old GLA KO mice showed less neurite outgrowth compared to neurons of WT mice.
source: We further determined the percentage of neurons with neurite outgrowth. Cultured DRG neurons of old GLA KO mice showed less neurite outgrowth compared to neurons of WT mice (p<0.001, Figure 3F).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of neurite outgrowth shown in Figure 3F with statistical significance p<0.001.

claim: TRPV1 gene expression did not differ between genotypes and age-groups.
source: While TRPV1 gene expression did not differ between genotypes and age-groups (Figure 4A), we found an increased number of TRPV1 immunoreactive DRG neurons in young and old GLA KO mice compared to their WT littermates (p<0.001 each, Figure 4B–F).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative real-time PCR data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Young GLA KO mice have an increased number of TRPV1 immunoreactive DRG neurons compared to young WT mice.
source: While TRPV1 gene expression did not differ between genotypes and age-groups (Figure 4A), we found an increased number of TRPV1 immunoreactive DRG neurons in young and old GLA KO mice compared to their WT littermates (p<0.001 each, Figure 4B–F).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry quantification shown in Figure 4B-F with statistical significance p<0.001.

claim: Old GLA KO mice have an increased number of TRPV1 immunoreactive DRG neurons compared to old WT mice.
source: While TRPV1 gene expression did not differ between genotypes and age-groups (Figure 4A), we found an increased number of TRPV1 immunoreactive DRG neurons in young and old GLA KO mice compared to their WT littermates (p<0.001 each, Figure 4B–F).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry quantification shown in Figure 4B-F with statistical significance p<0.001.

claim: TRPV1 immunoreactivity was mainly observed in small diameter neurons (<25 µm) independent of genotype and age.
source: We also analyzed the distribution of TRPV1 immunoreactivity across different neuronal sizes and quantified TRPV1 positive neuron diameters; neuron populations were stratified as small (<25 µm in diameter) and large (≥25 µm in diameter) neurons (Figure 4G)(Cesare and McNaughton, 1996; Hoheisel et al., 1994; Lawson et al., 1993). TRPV1 immunoreactivity was mainly observed in small diameter neurons independent of genotype and age.
evidence: This is supported by quantification of TRPV1 positive neuron diameters shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Cultured neurons appeared enlarged and carried deposits in GLA KO mice, while were of normal shape in WT mice.
source: Next, we investigated capsaicin induced TRPV1 current densities with patch-clamp analysis in five days old cultured DRG neurons. Neurons appeared enlarged and carried deposits in GLA KO mice, while were of normal shape in WT mice (Figure 4G,H).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy images shown in Figure 4H and 4I.

claim: There is a tendency for higher TRPV1 current densities in young GLA KO mice, but the difference is not significant between genotypes.
source: We observed a tendency for higher current densities in young GLA KO mice (exemplified current in Figure 4I), but the difference was not significant between genotypes (Figure 4J).
evidence: This is supported by patch-clamp analysis shown in Figure 4J.

claim: Cultured DRG neurons of old GLA KO and littermate WT mice did not respond to capsaicin at all.
source: In contrast, cultured DRG neurons of old GLA KO and littermate WT mice did not respond to capsaicin at all.
evidence: This is stated based on patch-clamp experiments.

claim: Old GLA KO mice showed heat hypersensitivity compared to baseline 24 hr after capsaicin injection.
source: Since increased neuronal TRPV1 protein expression may be associated with heat hypersensitivity, we determined paw withdrawal latencies after intraplantar injection of capsaicin in old GLA KO mice at a dose that induced only mild and short lasting pain behavior in WT mice (Carey et al., 2017; Sakurada et al., 1992). Indeed, old GLA KO mice showed heat hypersensitivity compared to baseline 24 hr after capsaicin (p<0.01 Figure 4L).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral testing data shown in Figure 4L with statistical significance p<0.01.

claim: HCN2 gene expression in DRG did not differ between genotypes and age-groups.
source: There was no intergroup difference for HCN2 gene expression in DRG of GLA KO and WT mice (Figure 5A), while HCN2 immunoreactivity increased with age in both genotypes (p<0.05, Figure 5B–F).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative real-time PCR data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: HCN2 immunoreactivity increased with age in both genotypes.
source: There was no intergroup difference for HCN2 gene expression in DRG of GLA KO and WT mice (Figure 5A), while HCN2 immunoreactivity increased with age in both genotypes (p<0.05, Figure 5B–F).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry quantification shown in Figure 5B-F with statistical significance p<0.05.

claim: Hyperpolarization-activated (Ih) current densities were markedly reduced in old GLA KO mice compared to old WT mice.
source: In contrast, patch-clamp analysis of DRG neurons revealed that hyperpolarization-activated (Ih) current densities (exemplified current in Figure 5G), which are carried by all four isoforms of HCN channels, were markedly reduced in old GLA KO mice compared to old WT mice (p<0.001 each, Figure 5H), but did not differ between mice of young age-groups.
evidence: This is supported by patch-clamp analysis shown in Figure 5H with statistical significance p<0.001.

claim: Ih current densities did not differ between young GLA KO and young WT mice.
source: In contrast, patch-clamp analysis of DRG neurons revealed that hyperpolarization-activated (Ih) current densities (exemplified current in Figure 5G), which are carried by all four isoforms of HCN channels, were markedly reduced in old GLA KO mice compared to old WT mice (p<0.001 each, Figure 5H), but did not differ between mice of young age-groups.
evidence: This is supported by patch-clamp analysis shown in Figure 5H.

claim: Heat hypersensitivity developed in old WT mice after CCI lasting up to day 28 after surgery.
source: Since HCN2 conditional knockout mice are protected from heat and mechanical hypersensitivity after peripheral nerve lesion (Emery et al., 2011), we applied chronic constriction injury (CCI) at the right sciatic nerve of GLA KO and WT littermates. Indeed, heat hypersensitivity only developed in old WT mice (p<0.01) lasting up to day 28 after surgery, while old GLA KO mice were spared (p<0.01, Figure 5I).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral testing data shown in Figure 5I with statistical significance p<0.01.

claim: Old GLA KO mice were spared from heat hypersensitivity after CCI.
source: Since HCN2 conditional knockout mice are protected from heat and mechanical hypersensitivity after peripheral nerve lesion (Emery et al., 2011), we applied chronic constriction injury (CCI) at the right sciatic nerve of GLA KO and WT littermates. Indeed, heat hypersensitivity only developed in old WT mice (p<0.01) lasting up to day 28 after surgery, while old GLA KO mice were spared (p<0.01, Figure 5I).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral testing data shown in Figure 5I with statistical significance p<0.01.

claim: Mechanical withdrawal thresholds remained at baseline level for the entire study period of 28 days in old GLA KO mice after CCI.
source: Also, mechanical withdrawal thresholds remained at baseline level for the entire study period of 28 days in old GLA KO mice, while WT mice displayed hypersensitivity to mechanical stimuli up to day 28 after CCI (p<0.01, Figure 5J).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral testing data shown in Figure 5J with statistical significance p<0.01.

claim: WT mice displayed hypersensitivity to mechanical stimuli up to day 28 after CCI.
source: Also, mechanical withdrawal thresholds remained at baseline level for the entire study period of 28 days in old GLA KO mice, while WT mice displayed hypersensitivity to mechanical stimuli up to day 28 after CCI (p<0.01, Figure 5J).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral testing data shown in Figure 5J with statistical significance p<0.01.

claim: Nav1.7 gene expression in DRG was not different in both age-groups and genotypes.
source: Nav1.7 gene expression in DRG was not different in both age-groups and genotypes (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative real-time PCR data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Nav1.7 protein expression in DRG did not differ between genotypes and age-groups.
source: Since Nav1.7 immunostaining failed using five different Nav1.7 antibodies detailed above, we applied enzyme-linked-immuno-sorbent assay on DRG samples and found no difference in Nav1.7 protein expression in DRG between genotypes and age-groups (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Sodium current densities were not different between young GLA KO and WT littermates.
source: Patch-clamp analysis revealed that sodium current densities (exemplified currents in Figure 6C) were not different between young GLA KO and WT littermates, but were notably reduced in old GLA KO mice compared to old WT mice (p<0.001 each, Figure 6D).
evidence: This is supported by patch-clamp analysis shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Sodium current densities were notably reduced in old GLA KO mice compared to old WT mice.
source: Patch-clamp analysis revealed that sodium current densities (exemplified currents in Figure 6C) were not different between young GLA KO and WT littermates, but were notably reduced in old GLA KO mice compared to old WT mice (p<0.001 each, Figure 6D).
evidence: This is supported by patch-clamp analysis shown in Figure 6D with statistical significance p<0.001.

claim: Sodium currents in DRG neurons from young GLA KO mice had normal fast inactivating kinetics at baseline.
source: We applied tetrodotoxin (TTX) to DRG neurons obtained from young GLA KO mice that had normal sodium currents with fast inactivating kinetics at baseline (black trace in Figure 6E).
evidence: This is supported by patch-clamp analysis shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Sodium currents in DRG neurons from young GLA KO mice were sensitive to TTX at a concentration of 100 nM.
source: These sodium currents were sensitive to TTX already at a concentration of 100 nM (red trace in Figure 6E) and recovered after washout with bath solution (grey trace in Figure 6E), such that the observed sodium currents were identified as being predominantly produced by Nav1.7, a channel which has been shown to contribute about 70% of the TTX sensitive current in small DRG neurons (Vasylyev et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by patch-clamp analysis shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Sodium currents recovered after washout with bath solution.
source: These sodium currents were sensitive to TTX already at a concentration of 100 nM (red trace in Figure 6E) and recovered after washout with bath solution (grey trace in Figure 6E), such that the observed sodium currents were identified as being predominantly produced by Nav1.7, a channel which has been shown to contribute about 70% of the TTX sensitive current in small DRG neurons (Vasylyev et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by patch-clamp analysis shown in Figure 6E.

claim: The observed sodium currents were identified as being predominantly produced by Nav1.7.
source: These sodium currents were sensitive to TTX already at a concentration of 100 nM (red trace in Figure 6E) and recovered after washout with bath solution (grey trace in Figure 6E), such that the observed sodium currents were identified as being predominantly produced by Nav1.7, a channel which has been shown to contribute about 70% of the TTX sensitive current in small DRG neurons (Vasylyev et al., 2014).
evidence: This is inferred from TTX sensitivity and supported by citation to Vasylyev et al., 2014.

claim: Nav1.7 contributes about 70% of the TTX sensitive current in small DRG neurons.
source: These sodium currents were sensitive to TTX already at a concentration of 100 nM (red trace in Figure 6E) and recovered after washout with bath solution (grey trace in Figure 6E), such that the observed sodium currents were identified as being predominantly produced by Nav1.7, a channel which has been shown to contribute about 70% of the TTX sensitive current in small DRG neurons (Vasylyev et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Vasylyev et al., 2014.

claim: Intraplantar injection of CFA led to heat hypersensitivity in all mice groups except for old GLA KO mice.
source: We then investigated whether reduced neuronal Nav1.7 currents may be associated with protection from heat and mechanical hypersensitivity in an inflammatory pain model, as known for Nav1.7 conditional knockout mice (Nassar et al., 2004). Indeed, intraplantar injection of complete Freund`s adjuvant (CFA) led to heat hypersensitivity in all mice groups except for old GLA KO mice (p<0.001, Figure 6F), in which heat withdrawal latencies did not change from baseline for the entire study period of seven days (p<0.001, Figure 6F).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral testing data shown in Figure 6F with statistical significance p<0.001.

claim: Heat withdrawal latencies did not change from baseline for the entire study period of seven days in old GLA KO mice after CFA injection.
source: We then investigated whether reduced neuronal Nav1.7 currents may be associated with protection from heat and mechanical hypersensitivity in an inflammatory pain model, as known for Nav1.7 conditional knockout mice (Nassar et al., 2004). Indeed, intraplantar injection of complete Freund`s adjuvant (CFA) led to heat hypersensitivity in all mice groups except for old GLA KO mice (p<0.001, Figure 6F), in which heat withdrawal latencies did not change from baseline for the entire study period of seven days (p<0.001, Figure 6F).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral testing data shown in Figure 6F with statistical significance p<0.001.

claim: All mice developed mechanical hypersensitivity starting one hour after CFA injection compared to baseline.
source: Similarly, all mice developed mechanical hypersensitivity starting one hour after CFA injection compared to baseline (p<0.001, Figure 6G), which was less pronounced in old GLA KO mice compared to old WT mice after CFA injection (Figure 6G), and all mice remained mechanically hypersensitive until day seven after CFA injection.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral testing data shown in Figure 6G with statistical significance p<0.001.

claim: Mechanical hypersensitivity was less pronounced in old GLA KO mice compared to old WT mice after CFA injection.
source: Similarly, all mice developed mechanical hypersensitivity starting one hour after CFA injection compared to baseline (p<0.001, Figure 6G), which was less pronounced in old GLA KO mice compared to old WT mice after CFA injection (Figure 6G), and all mice remained mechanically hypersensitive until day seven after CFA injection.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral testing data shown in Figure 6G.

claim: All mice remained mechanically hypersensitive until day seven after CFA injection.

claim: Gb3 is age-dependently associated with increased BiP expression indicating endoplasmic stress and nerve fiber degeneration.
source: We comprehensively investigated the impact of sensory neuron Gb3 deposits in the α-GAL deficient mouse model as a potential basis of small fiber neuropathy in FD and detected three major effects: Gb3 is age-dependently associated with (1) increased BiP expression indicating endoplasmic stress and nerve fiber degeneration, (2) increased neuronal TRPV1 protein expression and sustained capsaicin responsiveness in vivo, and (3) reduced neuronal Ih and Nav1.7 currents associated with a lack of thermal and mechanical hypersensitivity after nerve lesion and inflammation.
evidence: This is a summary statement supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Gb3 is age-dependently associated with increased neuronal TRPV1 protein expression and sustained capsaicin responsiveness in vivo.

claim: Exceeding compensation limits, Gb3 deposits might break loose from lysosomes getting into contact with other organelles and cellular structures.
source: We assessed Gb3 deposits in DRG of young and old GLA KO mice and show age-dependent intra- but also extra-cellular Gb3 accumulation challenging the concept of exclusive lysosomal storage. We hypothesize that exceeding compensation limits, Gb3 deposits might break loose from lysosomes getting into contact with other organelles and cellular structures.
